author: a. v. boyd
title: Thomas Vozzo discusses faith and business at Pepperdine University lecture
text:
Pepperdine University hosted Thomas Vozzo, former CEO and current senior advisor of Homeboy Industries, for a lecture on faith, service, and his experiences as an executive in both for-profit and nonprofit sectors on Apr. 1.
The event was part of the university’s Faith and Business Initiative, which aims to explore the intersection between theological principles and business practices. The initiative is supported by a $260,000 grant from the Templeton Foundation awarded in 2025.
During his remarks, Vozzo described his career path from serving as CEO of Aramark’s uniform and career apparel group to volunteering at Homeboy Industries—a nonprofit focused on reentry services for formerly incarcerated gang members. He explained that after years in a corporate environment focused primarily on shareholder value, he found new meaning working with people through Homeboy Industries. “I often think back to beatitudes, where Jesus says blessed are the poor in spirit, for they shall inherit the kingdom of heaven,” said Vozzo. “Jesus is talking about our people. They are authentic. They have, in my observation, a true sense of God. They are our guides and witnesses on how to find faith.”
Vozzo shared that his perspective shifted significantly while leading Homeboy Industries: “Once people heal, they love others,” he explained. “They love others when they learn to love themselves. And they love themselves when they find, deep down, that God loves them.” He encouraged attendees not to “Underlive life,” but instead live fully knowing their value.
Regan Schaffer, divisional dean of Seaver College’s Business Administration Division at Pepperdine University said: “Tom exemplifies the attributes of servant leadership that I seek to develop in my students… His story and his storytelling are so powerful that anytime is the right time for a visit from him.”
Jooho Lee, associate professor of business ethics and law at Seaver College added: “I can’t think of many places better than Pepperdine to study the relationship between business and the Christian faith… We look forward to continuing the conversation here in the coming years.”
The Faith and Business Initiative is led by three Seaver College faculty members—Schaffer; Chris Collins; and Lee—and will continue its programming over its three-year term.
